ideas.truth: For many Indian parents in their 50s+, the hardest part of a smartphone isn't using it — it's the fear of fumbling in front of family, especially when trying to see their children/grandchildren who live far away.
ideas.moment: A mother taps once, and instantly sees her son's face on a video call, sharp and bright, no confusion, no help needed.
ideas.key_frame: A silver-haired woman in a sunlit living room holds up the phone, her son's smiling face glowing clearly on the big screen, her own face lighting up in relief and joy.

ideas.truth: At this age, people don't want to look 'techy' — they want to look graceful, dignified, quietly premium, especially in front of their peers and children.
ideas.moment: At a family gathering, a father casually lifts his new phone to click one clean photo of everyone — no fuss, no adjusting, and the phone itself looks elegant in his hand.
ideas.key_frame: A well-dressed man in his 60s holds the phone at chest height, its metallic edge catching the light, family smiling behind him mid-laugh.

ideas.truth: Trust, for this generation, is built through simplicity — a product that doesn't ask them to learn anything new, that simply works the way life already does.
ideas.moment: The phone rests on a wooden table in golden evening light; one gentle tap and the screen wakes with large, clear icons — no clutter, no confusion.
ideas.key_frame: Close-up of the phone lying on a table, sunlight glinting off its camera module, screen blooming to life with big, legible icons.

why: It centers on the single strongest emotional trigger for this audience — staying connected with family — while naturally demonstrating screen clarity, ease of use, and camera quality without a word of jargon.
treatment: A warm, sunlit living room, early afternoon. An elderly woman sits with the new iPhone Duo in her hands. She taps the screen once — instantly her son's face appears, clear and bright, as if he's in the room. She smiles wide, genuinely moved, and says softly, 'Wow, so clear!' The moment lingers — real warmth, no tech talk. Then we cut close: her hand turns the phone slightly, sunlight catching its refined edge and camera as she takes one easy photo of her family gathered around her, the shutter sound soft and satisfying. The screen shows the photo instantly, crisp and beautiful. We end on the phone resting in her palm, calm and simple, as the name and a gentle tagline appear.

scenes.prompt: Warm, intimate handheld cinematic shot, soft natural afternoon light through sheer curtains. Subject: a warm Indian woman in her late 50s with silver-streaked hair tied in a neat bun, wearing a soft pastel cotton saree, thin gold bangles, and stylish reading glasses resting on her nose. She holds the phone in both hands and taps the screen once with her finger; the screen brightens and a video call connects, her face lighting up with a genuine, moved smile as she leans slightly toward the screen. Setting: a cozy Indian living room, marigold flowers on a side table, a family photo frame softly visible in the background. Style and ambience: real, tender, golden-hour realism — not glossy or artificial, like a candid home video with gentle documentary warmth. Ambient room tone, a faint breeze through curtains, soft notification chime as the call connects.
scenes.first_frame_still_prompt: The woman seated on a sofa, phone held up in both hands at chest height, screen glowing with a video call already connecting, soft golden afternoon light on her face, marigolds and a photo frame softly blurred behind her, warm and candid framing, phone matching reference exactly.

scenes.prompt: Same subject, same character description, word for word: a warm Indian woman in her late 50s with silver-streaked hair tied in a neat bun, wearing a soft pastel cotton saree, thin gold bangles, and stylish reading glasses resting on her nose. Soft camera shutter click, warm ambient room tone, gentle contented exhale from her.
on_screen_copy: Simple to use. Beautiful to hold.
